author: reek
body: blu's ASDE stage flew on the ASUS on 2026-08-04 and painted NOTHING. The cause was not a fault: with no link the stage went through e1000-phy-bring-up, whose e1000-await-aneg spends a million iterations and makes a full MDIC transaction on each, and a real MDIO transaction is tens of microseconds. Two arms of that is a minute or worse. Bounded, and indistinguishable from a hang to anyone watching a screen.

author: reek
body: A bench cable is normally out, so NO LINK IS THE NORMAL BENCH CONDITION and the arm below is the one that matters. -e1000-no-link is what makes the bed produce it, which was worth finding out: the failure had been called unreproducible here.

author: reek
body: What this asserts is that the stage COMPLETES on a dead link and says so. It cannot assert how long that takes -- a test that passes or fails on elapsed time on a shared box is a flaky test -- so the bound lives in the constants and this guards the observable half: every arm comes back, and comes back carrying a state that renders.

author: reek
body: The PHY is still reachable with the link down, so a nolink verdict must not be confused with an unreachable PHY. If this ever answers no, the give-up state is reporting the wrong thing.
